hero.title: The Nanda Dynasty: Magadha's Expansion
hero.description: The first 'Empire Builders' of ancient India, transitioning from territorial states to a pan-regional imperial power.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: The Nanda era signifies the bridge between the Haryanka-Shishunaga period and the Mauryan Empire.

cards.details: Mahapadma Nanda overthrows the Shishunaga dynasty, establishing the Nanda rule.
Alexander the Great invades the Indus valley; the might of the Nanda army reportedly deterred his troops from eastward advancement.
Chandragupta Maurya, guided by Chanakya, overthrows Dhana Nanda, marking the end of the dynasty.

items.title: M.U.S.T
items.decryption: Mahapadma (founder), known as Ugrasena, introduced standardized weights/measures and a rigorous taxation system.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Mistaking the Nandas for Kshatriyas; Puranic sources clearly label them as 'Sarvakshatrantaka' (destroyers of Kshatriyas) and Shudra origin.
Assuming Alexander defeated the Nandas; historical evidence suggests the Nanda army's strength was the reason Alexander's soldiers refused to move further east.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Centered in Magadha (Pataliputra)
  • Expanded into Kalinga (Odisha) and Deccan
  • Control over major trade routes

Personalities

  • Mahapadma Nanda: The Conqueror
  • Dhana Nanda: The Last Ruler
  • Chanakya: The Diplomatic Catalyst

Core Structural Overview

  • Political Centralization: Shift from Gana-Sangha to Absolute Monarchy.
  • Military Prowess: Greek sources cite 200,000 infantry, 80,000 cavalry, 8,000 chariots, and 6,000 elephants.
  • Economic Reforms: Introduction of 'Karshapana' (punched-marked coins) and systematic tax collection.
